### Florence Renaissance and Culinary Context
This itinerary is designed for three adults with a focus on accessible Renaissance masterpieces and traditional Tuscan dining. The daily budget of €200 per person comfortably covers high-end museum entries, taxi or bus transport, and premium dining experiences. All selected activities avoid steep climbs or strenuous hiking, utilizing elevators where available and focusing on ground-level exploration.

### 5-Day Florence Cultural Schedule
Day 1: The Heart of the Renaissance
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/62/Florence_Duomo_from_Michelangelo_Square.jpg/1200px-Florence_Duomo_from_Michelangelo_Square.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Explore the Piazza del Duomo, including the interior of the Cathedral and the Baptistery's golden doors.
- Afternoon: Visit the San Lorenzo Leather Market for high-quality Italian craftsmanship and souvenirs.
- Dinner: Trattoria Mario — Famous for authentic **Ribollita** and a lively, traditional atmosphere.
Action: [Button: View Market Map] https://www.mercatocentrale.com/florence/

Day 2: Michelangelo and Sacred Art
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/David_von_Michelangelo.jpg/1200px-David_von_Michelangelo.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/star.svg
- Morning: View Michelangelo’s David at the Accademia Gallery (advance booking essential).
- Afternoon: Tour the Basilica di Santa Croce, the burial place of Michelangelo, Galileo, and Machiavelli.
- Dinner: Regina Bistecca — Specializes in the iconic **Bistecca alla Fiorentina**, served by weight.
Action: [Button: Accademia Tickets] https://www.galleriaaccademiafirenze.it/en/

Day 3: The Oltrarno Artisan District
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Palazzo_pitti_08.jpg/1200px-Palazzo_pitti_08.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Visit the Pitti Palace and its Palatine Gallery to see works by Raphael and Titian.
- Afternoon: Wander the Oltrarno neighborhood to visit active workshops of goldsmiths and bookbinders.
- Dinner: Osteria Santo Spirito — Known for truffle gnocchi and traditional **Pappardelle sulla Lepre**.
Action: [Button: Explore Oltrarno] https://www.visitflorence.com/itineraries-in-florence/oltrarno-neighborhood.html

Day 4: Tuscan Hillside Excursion
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Fiesole_Teatro_Romano_2.jpg/1200px-Fiesole_Teatro_Romano_2.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Morning: Take Bus #7 from Piazza San Marco to Fiesole (20 mins) to see the Roman Theater and Etruscan ruins.
- Afternoon: Return to Florence for the Mercato Nuovo and the "Porcellino" bronze boar for good luck.
- Dinner: Trattoria Da Rocco — Located in the Sant'Ambrogio Market, offering seasonal **Pappa al Pomodoro**.
Action: [Button: Fiesole Bus Info] https://www.at-bus.it/en

Day 5: Masterpieces of the Uffizi
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/Uffizi_Gallery_Florence_Italy.jpg/1200px-Uffizi_Gallery_Florence_Italy.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Extensive tour of the Uffizi Gallery, home to Botticelli’s "Birth of Venus" and Da Vinci’s works.
- Afternoon: A final stroll across the Ponte Vecchio and a visit to the Ferragamo Shoe Museum for fashion history.
- Dinner: Buca Lapi — Set in a historic cellar, serving premium Tuscan steaks and local Chianti Classico.
Action: [Button: Uffizi Gallery Info] https://www.uffizi.it/en/the-uffizi
